title: Beyond Red Lines: The Emergence of Euralarm and the European Fire and Security Industry (1970-2020)
author: Simone Fari, Graham Hollister-Short, Pernille Roldgaard, Florian T. Furtak
target_audience: Professionals and historians in fire and security industries
Policy makers and regulators in safety industry
core_themes: Development of fire and security industry in Europe
Role and emergence of Euralarm as an industry association
primary_purpose: To provide a comprehensive historical account of the formation, evolution, and influence of Euralarm over fifty years, charting its role in shaping European fire detection, alarm, and security industries and their regulatory environments.

structure_format.narrative_style: Academic and analytical, with historical case studies
structure_format.organization: Chronological and thematic, highlighting major industry milestones, regulatory turning points, and the impact of Euralarm on policy and technical developments
features: Appendices with technical standards and regulations

key_concepts_lessons: The harmonization of standards across European markets is essential for industry growth.
Industry associations like Euralarm are crucial intermediaries among businesses, governments, and consumers.
Fire and security technology have evolved rapidly due to regulatory and technical innovation.
Collaboration across national and corporate boundaries shapes the trajectory of safety industries.
Business interests and public safety goals must be balanced in industry policymaking.
notable_features: First thorough account of Euralarm and its role
Blends business, technological, and policy analysis
Focus on cooperation and conflict across the European market
Utilization of previously unpublished archival materials
cultural_historical_context: The work covers 1970–2020, a period during which Europe experienced increased industrial collaboration, regulatory integration (especially through EU mechanisms), and technological advancement in life safety. The history is set against broad currents such as European integration and global competition in electronics and safety systems.
reception_impact: Praised in academic circles for filling a gap in European industrial history
Referenced by policy makers and industry professionals examining regulatory and standardization issues
Recognized as a key contribution to understanding postwar European industry collaboration
Primarily used as a reference in specialized fields, but of growing interest to those studying business associations
comparable_titles: The Market for Political Economy: The Advent of Regulation in the European Union by Susanne K. Schmidt
Standardization in History: A Critical Review of Gender and Technical Standards by Ursula Huws (ed.)
The European Rescue of the Nation-State by Alan Milward
